scene:
Three areas side by side, read left to right. Do not write any title or heading above any area.

On the left: four small panels stacked from top to bottom, each a little deeper than the one above, with one simple drawing each. Top panel: two separate product boxes joined only by a handshake, labelled SALES AGREEMENT. Second panel: two product boxes standing on one shared shelf, labelled SHARED SERVICES. Third panel: two product boxes joined by a pipe with arrows both ways, labelled CONNECTED WORKFLOWS. Bottom panel: a single merged product box, labelled ONE PRODUCT. To the right of the four panels, a single card with a large question mark, labelled WHICH BENEFIT?, with thin arrows from each of the four panels pointing to it.

In the centre: a two-pan balance scale tipped down on its right side. The raised left pan holds a small stack of calendar pages labelled 26 WEEKS AVAILABLE. The lower right pan holds a taller stack of work boxes; the single label 29 WEEKS NEEDED appears once, above that stack only. Below the scale, a short queue: a work box with two engineer figures and a large ochre check mark, labelled INTEGRATION FIRST; beside it a box set aside on a bench with a small hourglass, labelled PORTAL WAITS.

On the right, upper half: two bars side by side on a baseline. A short teal bar labelled €400K CHARGED. A taller ochre stacked bar with two segments: a large lower segment labelled €700K/YEAR and a small upper segment labelled +€300K ONCE.
On the right, lower half: a horizontal timeline arrow pointing right with three milestones in order left to right: a pen signing a document labelled 31 MAR: RESERVE; a clipboard with a test tick labelled MAY: TEST; a pair of scissors cutting a thin ribbon labelled 31 MAY: LAST FREE CANCEL.

TEXT: draw exactly these labels, each once and nothing else: SALES AGREEMENT, SHARED SERVICES, CONNECTED WORKFLOWS, ONE PRODUCT, WHICH BENEFIT?, 26 WEEKS AVAILABLE, 29 WEEKS NEEDED, INTEGRATION FIRST, PORTAL WAITS, €400K CHARGED, €700K/YEAR, +€300K ONCE, 31 MAR: RESERVE, MAY: TEST, 31 MAY: LAST FREE CANCEL. No headings or titles of any kind, no axis numbers, no names under figures. Any other text is a defect.
alt: Left, four panels of rising integration depth, sales agreement, shared services, connected workflows and one product, all pointing to a question card asking which benefit; middle, a balance shows 29 engineer-weeks needed outweighing 26 available, with the integration placed first and the portal set aside to wait; right, a bar of €400K charged by the parent beside a taller stack of €700K a year plus €300K once, above a timeline of 31 March reserve, May test and 31 May last free cancel.
caption: Choose integration depth for a named benefit, decide what waits for scarce engineers, and price and reserve the route to independence before the parent’s services stop.
